clue.text: Stone-age foresight?

blocks.note: surface reading: what cave dwellers could predict
setter's reading: the Stone Age came before science

explanation.surface: A wondering aside about whether cave people could see what lay ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PRE-SCIENCE: the Stone Age was a time before science, which is the joke behind the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescience is knowledge of events before they happen, which is exactly what foresight means.

clue.text: Goals for some who crawl

blocks.note: surface reading: the targets of babies or insects that move on all fours
setter's reading: drinkers on a crawl, a tour of drinking houses one after another

explanation.surface: Wondering what a crawling creature is heading for.
explanation.walkthrough: A pub crawl is a British night out moving from bar to bar, so the places visited are the goals.
explanation.definitionFit: On a pub crawl the drinkers' destinations, one after another, are the bars themselves.

clue.text: Old Master comes up for a short test

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: ex- means former
MA, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A painting by an Old Master is brought out for a quick examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Master' looks like one phrase meaning a great painter; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the clipped form of examination, a test, so it is itself a short word.

clue.text: Perfection in addition, after study

indicators.note: placing one piece after another fixes the order in which they are joined

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
summation is the act of adding up

explanation.surface: A student achieving flawless arithmetic after revising.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummation is the completion or crowning point of something, its ultimate fulfilment or perfect state.

clue.text: And this, with Brutus, seen as honourable!

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a code of what is held right, while the phrase reads adjectivally

indicators.note: Brutus was a Roman, so the words beside him are to be put into his Latin tongue

blocks.note: Latin for and
Latin for this

explanation.surface: An echo of Mark Antony's refrain that Brutus is an honourable man.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar, Antony repeats 'Brutus is an honourable man'; the clue asks for 'and this' said as Brutus would, in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle, the standard by which conduct is judged right and worthy of respect.

clue.text: Business with many fell away and folded up

blocks.note: CO, abbreviation for company
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
to lapse is to fall away or decline

explanation.surface: A firm lost many customers, then went under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins CO to the many.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has collapsed has caved in, the way a firm or a deckchair folds up.

clue.text: Like the ewe lamb, . or the pearl of great price

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, costly, while this is a noun phrase

blocks.note: first meaning: beloved, as the poor man's lamb in Nathan's parable was to him
second meaning: expensive, as the gospel pearl that cost the merchant all he had

explanation.walkthrough: Both pictures are biblical: Nathan's parable in 2 Samuel tells of a ewe lamb that 'was unto him as a daughter', and Matthew tells of a pearl worth everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both beloved and costly, and each biblical image illustrates one of those two senses.

clue.text: I'm batting, exultant, all round? “Out!”

indicators.note: a word that goes all round others wraps them inside itself

blocks.note: first part of ELATED, exultant
taken as written without the apostrophe
in cricket the side batting is in
rest of ELATED, wrapping round the others

explanation.surface: A batsman exults about being at the crease, only to hear the umpire's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The exultant word is split to wrap round the other two. In cricket the side batting is said to be 'in'; a dismissed batsman is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who is out has been knocked out of the game, removed from further play.

clue.text: In tree development plant- groups are given new life

definitions.note: regenerate is used here as an adjective, reborn

indicators.note: development changes the form of something, so these letters are rearranged
one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: the letters of tree rearranged
genera are groups of related plant species

explanation.surface: Botanical groups find new vigour as a tree develops.
explanation.walkthrough: GENERA sits inside the rearranged TREE: RE-GENERA-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective regenerate means spiritually reborn or restored, renewed in vigour.

clue.text: As Athene with Zeus, so Wendy with Barrie

definitions.text: As Athene with Zeus, so Wendy with Barrie

blocks.note: the goddess sprang fully formed from the head of her father
J M Barrie's character in Peter Pan was a product of his imagination

explanation.walkthrough: Athene was literally born from Zeus's head; Wendy was figuratively born in Barrie's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an original idea or creation, literally an offspring of someone's mind.

clue.text: But at cards one's higher than he

definitions.text: But at cards one's higher than he

blocks.clueFragment: But at cards one's higher than he
blocks.note: surface reading: someone generally supreme who is outranked only in a card game
setter's reading: one is the ace, which ranks above a monarch in most card games

explanation.walkthrough: A monarch normally outranks everybody, but in a pack of cards the ace, card number one, beats him.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch is the highest of men, yet the ace ranks above his picture card in most games.

clue.text: Auburn rustics amazed “That one small head could carry all he knew

definitions.text: Auburn rustics amazed “That one small head could carry all he knew

blocks.note: surface reading: red-haired country folk astonished at someone

blocks.clueFragment: That one small head could carry all he knew
blocks.note: setter's reading: a line from Goldsmith's poem The Deserted Village, about the village teacher

explanation.walkthrough: Auburn is the village of Goldsmith's The Deserted Village; its rustics gazed in wonder 'That one small head could carry all he knew' about the local teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: In Goldsmith's poem the learned figure who astonished the villagers was the man who taught their children.

clue.text: What may bring prices down in the sales

definitions.text: What may bring prices down in the sales

blocks.clueFragment: What may bring prices down in the sales
blocks.note: surface reading: whatever cuts prices in a shop sale
setter's reading: a sale by bidding where the price starts high and drops until someone accepts

explanation.walkthrough: In this kind of auction the auctioneer starts high and lowers the price step by step, the reverse of a normal auction.
explanation.definitionFit: This auction method begins at a high asking figure and lowers it until a buyer accepts.

clue.text: Falsify a deal? Utter nonsense!

indicators.note: making nonsense of the words jumbles them into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that the charge of rigging a business deal is complete rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective intensifying the nonsense; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to make impure by mixing in inferior matter, a way of corrupting or faking.

clue.text: Satisfied with a few words in translation

blocks.note: demands are met when satisfied
taken as written
a phrase is a short group of words

explanation.surface: Someone content to express things briefly when translating.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphrase is a literal, word-for-word rendering of a text into another language.

clue.text: Lacking entertainment on night of June 24

definitions.text: Lacking entertainment on night of June 24

blocks.clueFragment: Lacking entertainment on night of June 24
blocks.note: surface reading: a dull evening with no show on a summer date
setter's reading: Shakespeare's comedy set on Midsummer night, Midsummer Day being June 24

explanation.walkthrough: Midsummer Day falls on June 24, so the entertainment is A Midsummer Night's Dream; lacking that play's last word gives sleep without visions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep without any visions is the literal meaning, here reached through missing the Shakespeare comedy.

clue.text: Abridge so record is in one volume .. .

indicators.note: one piece is set inside another

blocks.note: EP, an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
a tome is a large book
taken as written, placed inside the book

explanation.surface: Condensing a record into a single book.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes before the book's last letter rather than dead centre. The dots link to 21-down, whose clue continues this one.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise is to make a condensed summary or digest of a longer work.

clue.text: Broadcaster delighted to be walking thus?

definitions.note: the answer describes a broadcaster at work rather than naming one
the answer is the manner of walking, not the delight itself

blocks.note: first meaning: what a broadcaster is while transmitting live
second meaning: how a delighted person is said to walk, light-footed with joy

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'walking on air' means elated; the same two words describe a broadcaster who is live.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who is transmitting live is described as being heard over the radio waves.

clue.text: This said to expedite mending process, anyhow at this

definitions.text: This said to expedite mending process
definitions.note: the answer is the missing word of a proverb, not a synonym of the phrase
the answer completes the phrase rather than replacing it

blocks.clueFragment: This said to expedite mending process
blocks.note: first meaning: the proverb holds that the less said, the soonest things are mended
second meaning: the phrase 'at ...' means in any case, anyhow

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Least said, soonest mended'; 'at least' means anyhow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes both the proverb about quarrels healing and the stock phrase meaning in any case.

clue.text: Enjoy drinks with National Trust — how permissive!

blocks.note: to indulge is to treat oneself, often to drink
NT, the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Visitors to a heritage property having a drink, and how lax the rules are.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses in Britain; NT is its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone indulgent is lenient and readily allows others what they want.

clue.text: Go in the local, upset about the races

indicators.note: something upset is knocked out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A punter heads into the pub, upset over the horse races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The races' suggests horse racing; here it means human peoples. The local is British slang for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnology is the study of peoples and their cultures, so the adjective concerns human races.

clue.text: ... . result, publication

blocks.note: first meaning: an outcome
second meaning: one number of a magazine

explanation.walkthrough: The dots continue 16-down's clue; this answer is the third word in the chain, with two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an outcome of events and one numbered edition of a periodical.

clue.text: Chaff about one revel

indicators.note: one word goes about, that is around, another

blocks.note: chaff and rot both mean worthless talk
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.definitionFit: To run riot or have a riot is to make merry wildly, a noisy spree.

clue.text: Oath used by renegades

indicators.note: the letters wanted are those employed inside the next word

blocks.note: the middle of the word

explanation.definitionFit: It is a mild old-fashioned exclamation, a minced form of 'by God', so a sort of swear.

clue.text: Whale-hunting 10 in the Bible?

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the whale-hunting captain

blocks.note: first meaning: the captain who chases Moby Dick in Melville's novel
second meaning: the answer to 10 is a monarch, and a wicked one of Israel bears this name

explanation.walkthrough: Melville's whaling captain shares his name with the biblical ruler of Israel married to Jezebel.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical ruler of Israel, husband of Jezebel, bears this name, as does Melville's sea captain.

clue.text: Item One on the agenda before doing anything else

blocks.note: first meaning: the opening matter on a list
second meaning: early, at the very start of the day

explanation.walkthrough: One phrase read literally names an opening item, and idiomatically means early, as in 'first thing tomorrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the opening item on a list, and idiomatically meaning promptly at the start of the day.

clue.text: Openings in the East, certainly

blocks.note: E, abbreviation for east
yes is an emphatic affirmative, certainly

explanation.surface: Opportunities in the Orient, without a doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Small holes such as those in a needle or for laces are called by this name.

clue.text: Sang, being famous

blocks.note: first meaning: performed a mass or praised in song
second meaning: renowned

explanation.walkthrough: A priest celebrates mass, often by singing it; the same word as an adjective means renowned.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means praised or performed a rite, and as an adjective it means widely renowned.
